MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Two half turns together make (1 mark)
   A. a full turn
   B. a half turn
   C. a quarter turn
   D. two full turns

2. Estimate 5,064 − 1,927 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 3,120
   B. 3,130
   C. 3,230
   D. 3,140

3. Change 72 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 1.2 days
   B. 3 days
   C. 4 days
   D. 6 days

4. Work out 8,421 − 6,537. (1 mark)
   A. 1,894
   B. 2,116
   C. 1,884
   D. 1,784

5. In the fraction 2/3, what does the numerator 2 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. The size of each part in centimetres
   B. The number of wholes
   C. How many of the equal parts are taken
   D. How many equal parts the whole has

6. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 5 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 15 blocks
   B. 25 blocks
   C. 130 blocks
   D. 125 blocks

7. A rectangle is made of 9 rows with 4 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 45 square units
   B. 36 square units
   C. 26 square units
   D. 13 square units

8. What is the rule of the pattern 1,200, 1,500, 1,800, 2,100? (1 mark)
   A. add 1,200
   B. add 300
   C. add 600
   D. subtract 300

9. What is 250 cm in metres? (1 mark)
   A. 2.5 m
   B. 2.05 m
   C. 25 m
   D. 0.25 m

10. What is 7 m 5 cm − 1 m 48 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 57 cm
   B. 5 m 67 cm
   C. 5 m 47 cm
   D. 5 m 57 cm

11. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many are mango or pawpaw together? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 6
   C. 5
   D. 7

12. What is the total value of the digit 9 in 3,907? (1 mark)
   A. 9,000
   B. 900
   C. 9
   D. 90

13. Beth writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 2/9
   B. 3 1/2
   C. 13/6
   D. 11/5

14. How long is a lesson that starts at 10:30 a.m. and ends at 2:15 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 55 min
   B. 4 h 45 min
   C. 3 h 45 min
   D. 3 h 30 min

15. What is 700 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 70
   C. 700
   D. 8

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Tabitha cuts a 7 m 20 cm rope into 6 pieces of equal length. Find the length of one piece. (3 marks)

17. Find the volume of a cube with sides of 4 blocks. (3 marks)

18. Write the four facts that belong to an array of 3 rows with 8 dots in each row. (4 marks)

19. Write three reasons why we prepare a shopping list. (3 marks)

20. Write 2 25/100 and 5 7/100 as decimals. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — a full turn
   Two halves make one whole turn.

2. B — 3,130
   5,064 rounds to 5,060 and 1,927 rounds to 1,930. 5,060 − 1,930 = 3,130.

3. B — 3 days
   72 ÷ 24 = 3 days.

4. C — 1,884
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 8,421 − 6,537 = 1,884. Check: 1,884 + 6,537 = 8,421.

5. C — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 2/3 it says that 2 parts are taken.

6. D — 125 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 5 = 25 blocks. There are 5 layers, so the volume is 25 × 5 = 125 blocks.

7. B — 36 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 9 × 4 = 36 square units.

8. B — add 300
   Each number is 300 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 300.

9. A — 2.5 m
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 250 cm in metres is 2.5 m.

10. D — 5 m 57 cm
   705 − 148 = 557 cm = 5 m 57 cm.

11. C — 5
   4 + 1 = 5.

12. B — 900
   The digit 9 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 9 × 100 = 900.

13. B — 3 1/2
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 3 1/2.

14. C — 3 h 45 min
   Count on from 10:30 a.m. to 2:15 p.m.. The total is 3 h 45 min.

15. A — 7
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 700 ÷ 100 = 7.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 720 ÷ 6 = 120 cm (2 marks); 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm (1 mark).

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: 64 blocks
   Working / marking points: 4 × 4 = 16 per layer (1 mark); 16 × 4 (1 mark); 64 blocks (1 mark).

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3 × 8 = 24, 8 × 3 = 24, 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: To remember everything we need; to buy only what is needed; to avoid spending more than we have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason, up to 3 marks.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2.25 and 5.07
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal. 5 7/100 needs a 0 in the tenths place.
